Only premium yield passes. The weekly RSI at 36.3 is the critical red flag — GOOG appears to be in early recovery from a pullback. Selling calls now risks capping upside during a recovery rally toward the $398 high.
**Verdict:** Do NOT sell calls here. Weekly RSI signals potential recovery. If GOOG rallies toward $370+ with daily RSI >65, revisit. Selling calls during a recovery is the classic mistake of giving away upside for thin premium.

# NVDA Options Analysis — 2026-08-17
**Price:** $227.42 | **RSI(D/W):** 76.2/51.1 | **IV Rank:** ~68%
**200 MA:** $194.88 (+16.7%) | **52w High:** $235.47 (pullback 3.4%)
**ATM IV:** 38.3% | **Hist Vol:** 36.9% | **Nearest expiry:** Sep 18, 2026 (32 DTE)

## 1. Strategy Selector
**IV Environment:** Elevated (68th percentile) — premium selling is attractive.
**RSI read:** Daily 76.2 (overbought!), Weekly 51.1 (neutral). Stock just 3.4% from 52w high — approaching resistance.
**Flowchart:** IV HIGH → premium selling strategies favored. Stock OVERBOUGHT on daily, near all-time highs → IDEAL for covered calls. Not a CSP setup (stock extended upward, not pulling back to support).
**Recommendation:** SELL COVERED CALLS — textbook setup. Stock overbought, IV elevated, near resistance. CSPs contraindicated (you want to sell puts into weakness, not strength). LEAPs contraindicated (near highs, IV expensive, no discount).

## 2. Cash-Secured Put — Entry Condition Check
□ IV RANK ≥ 40: ✅ (68%)
□ DAILY RSI ≤ 40: ❌ (76.2 — deeply overbought, opposite of what CSPs need)
□ PRICE near support: ❌ (16.7% above 200 MA — far from any support)
□ PREMIUM yield ≥ 1.0%: ✅ ($205 put at $2.76/205 = 1.35%)

**Score: 2/4 → 🟡 MARGINAL**
IV is elevated making premium attractive, but the setup is wrong. RSI 76.2 means the stock is extended — selling puts into strength means you'd be establishing a put position at a poor entry point. If NVDA reverses from this overbought level, your put moves against you quickly.
**Verdict:** Skip CSP. Wait for pullback. If NVDA corrects to $200-210 range (near 200 MA at $195) with RSI <40, that would be a 4/4 green-light CSP setup with excellent premium from elevated IV.

## 3. Covered Call — Entry Condition Check
□ IV RANK ≥ 40: ✅ (68% — elevated, premium is rich)
□ DAILY RSI ≥ 60: ✅ (76.2 — overbought, stock extended)
□ WEEKLY RSI overbought or near resistance: ✅ (price 3.4% from 52w high $235.47 — clear resistance zone)
□ PREMIUM yield ≥ 0.8%: ✅ ($240 call at $5.55/$227.42 = 2.44%)

**Score: 4/4 → 🟢 GOOD SETUP**

**Full Strike Analysis:**
• **Resistance levels:** $235.47 (52w high), $240 (psychological/strike concentration)
• **Recommended strikes:**
  - **Conservative:** $245 (7.7% OTM, ~0.20 delta) — $4.10 premium (1.8% yield/32 DTE)
  - **Aggressive:** $240 (5.5% OTM, ~0.25 delta) — $5.55 premium (2.44% yield/32 DTE)
• **Open interest:** Excellent liquidity — $240 has 55,243 OI, $245 has 33,398 OI
• **If called away at $240:** You sell at $240 + collect $5.55 premium. If basis is near current ($227), total return = $18.13/share (8% in 32 days).
• **If called away at $245:** You sell at $245 + collect $4.10 premium. Total return = $21.68/share (9.5% in 32 days).
• **Assessment:** This is the best setup across all three tickers today. Stock is overbought, approaching its 52w high resistance, IV is elevated making premium rich. Whether NVDA stalls at $235-240 resistance (likely given RSI) or breaks through, you're collecting 1.8-2.4% in a month. Probability of profit (keeping premium) is ~75-80%.

**Risk to flag:** If NVDA breaks convincingly above $236 on an AI catalyst (earnings beat, new product cycle), it could run past your strike. The $245 strike gives more breathing room. If you want max safety, $250 at $3.16 (1.4% yield) sits above the psychological $250 level.

## 4. LEAPS Entry Monitor
**NVDA $227.42 | Score: 1/6 🔴 NO SETUP**
• RSI Daily ≤35: ❌ (76.2 — overbought)
• Weekly RSI stabilizing after decline: ❌ (not declining, stock trending up)
• Price within 5% of support: ❌ (16.7% above 200 MA)
• IV Rank <30: ❌ (68% — expensive)
• Options liquid: ✅ (extremely liquid, tight spreads)
• Pullback ≥15%: ❌ (only 3.4% from high)

**No LEAPS setup.** Stock is near all-time highs with elevated IV — the exact opposite of a LEAPS buying opportunity. LEAPs purchased here would carry maximum vega risk (IV mean-reversion would crush your position) and zero discount.
**Trigger to watch:** NVDA needs a 15%+ pullback (to ~$200) with IV cooling below 30% before LEAPs become interesting. That setup might emerge after a broader market correction or an earnings disappointment.

# TSLA Options Analysis — 2026-08-17
**Price:** $340.80 | **RSI(D/W):** 70.6/34.2 | **IV Rank:** ~26%
**200 MA:** $405.48 (-16.0% below) | **52w High:** $489.88 (pullback 30.4%)
**ATM IV:** 38.5% | **Hist Vol:** 46.5% | **Nearest expiry:** Sep 18, 2026 (32 DTE)

## 1. Strategy Selector
**IV Environment:** Low (26th percentile) — premium selling offers thin reward.
**RSI read:** Daily 70.6 (overbought, bounce underway), Weekly 34.2 (still oversold from macro decline). Stock 30.4% below 52w high, 16% below 200 MA — deep pullback territory but bouncing.
**Flowchart:** IV LOW → premium selling less attractive, favor buying strategies. Stock in BOUNCE from deep pullback → conflicting signals (daily overbought but weekly still low). This is a transitional phase.
**Recommendation:** MONITOR for LEAPS. The deep pullback (30.4%) combined with low IV (26%) makes TSLA the best LEAPS candidate. However, daily RSI at 70.6 means the initial bounce has already happened — wait for consolidation/pullback before entering. Don't chase.

## 2. Cash-Secured Put — Entry Condition Check
□ IV RANK ≥ 40: ❌ (26% — premium is thin)
□ DAILY RSI ≤ 40: ❌ (70.6 — overbought, already bounced)
□ PRICE near support: ❌ (between levels — 14% above $298 low, 16% below $405 MA)
□ PREMIUM yield ≥ 1.0%: ✅ ($310 put at $4.15/310 = 1.34%)

**Score: 1/4 → 🔴 SKIP**
TSLA has bounced from its ~$298 low and is now overbought on daily RSI. The ideal CSP window was when RSI was <30 near the low. Current setup is wrong on 3 of 4 criteria.
**Verdict:** Do not sell puts here. You'd be selling into a bounce (RSI 70.6) with low IV (thin premium for the risk). If TSLA retests $300-310 with IV expansion, that would be a proper CSP opportunity.

## 3. Covered Call — Entry Condition Check
□ IV RANK ≥ 40: ❌ (26% — IV is low, premium relatively thin given TSLA's volatility)
□ DAILY RSI ≥ 60: ✅ (70.6 — overbought)
□ WEEKLY RSI overbought or near resistance: ❌ (34.2 — deeply oversold, stock in recovery)
□ PREMIUM yield ≥ 0.8%: ✅ ($370 call at $6.35/$340.80 = 1.86%)

**Score: 2/4 → 🟡 MARGINAL**
The daily RSI and premium yield pass, but the critical misses are: (1) IV is low at 26%, meaning you're selling cheap premium — giving away upside for small reward; (2) Weekly RSI at 34.2 signals TSLA is recovering from a deep oversold condition, not topping out. Capping upside at $370 means limiting recovery potential toward the $405 200 MA.
**Verdict:** Only sell calls here if you actively want to reduce TSLA exposure. The premium ($6.35 at $370) sounds decent in absolute terms but in the context of TSLA's 46% historical vol and deep oversold weekly, you're likely selling too cheap and too early in the recovery.

## 4. LEAPS Entry Monitor
**TSLA $340.80 | Score: 4/6 🟢 LEAPS ALERT (conditional)**
• RSI Daily ≤35: ❌ (70.6 — already bounced, missed the bottom)
• Weekly RSI stabilizing after decline: ✅ (34.2 oversold, daily RSI bounce confirms stabilization)
• Price within 5% of support: ❌ (no clear immediate support — $298 low is 14% below)
• IV Rank <30: ✅ (26% — options are relatively cheap!)
• Options liquid: ✅ (TSLA extremely liquid: $360 LEAPS bid/ask $66.20/$67.45, spread 1.9%)
• Pullback ≥15%: ✅ (30.4% — massive pullback from $489.88 high)

**Score hits 4/6 — but important context:**
The daily RSI at 70.6 means you've already missed the initial bounce from $298 to $340 (+14%). Buying LEAPs here means chasing the bounce, not catching the bottom. The IDEAL entry would have been 2-3 weeks ago when RSI was <30 near $300.

**Conditional LEAPS Plan (act on pullback, not today):**
• Wait for: Daily RSI to reset below 40 via consolidation ($310-325 range)
• Target strike: $380 (~10% OTM from current, ~6% below 200 MA)
• Expiry: Sep 17, 2027 (395 DTE)
• Current premium: $59.25-60.35 per contract
• Breakeven: ~$440 (29% above current — needs conviction)
• Thesis: TSLA recovers toward 200 MA ($405) and beyond over 12 months
• Thesis breakers: Continued demand erosion, political risk acceleration, break below $280

**Why this is a 🟢 with a wait:**
The structural conditions for a LEAPS entry are present (deep pullback, cheap IV, liquid market). What's missing is the tactical timing — RSI 70.6 says "wait for a pullback within the pullback." A consolidation to $310-325 with RSI resetting to 35-40 would be the trigger. Set alerts and be patient.
